subject: Mutual Action Plan + Acceptance test catalog — next steps and owners
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 16:23:00 -0400
Subject: Mutual Action Plan + Acceptance test catalog — next steps and owners

Emily — following our product walkthrough today, attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an acceptance "smoke" test catalog that maps to the MAP milestones. Key asks in this note: please confirm the gating priorities and assign an internal owner for each acceptance line.

High-level suggested MAP (milestones & exit gates):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): Integration requirements, data access, and environment provisioning. Exit gate: test workspace available, telemetry hook validated.
- Week 1–2 (Baseline): Ingest sample dataset, run smoke validation. Exit gate: 95% of sample payloads accepted, end-to-end latency under SLO for sample size.
- Week 3–4 (Feature validation): Model prompts + routing policy tests, privacy checks. Exit gate: pass of critical functional test set AND SOC2 evidence checklist items completed.
- Week 5 (Pilot): 1% live traffic routing for controlled evaluation. Exit gate: error rate <1% over 48 hours, resource usage within expected budget, agreement on cutover date.

Acceptance tests we included (attached acceptance-smoke-suite.csv) are intentionally focused and automatable: connectivity, tokenization parity, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), correctness on curated prompts, and KV cache warm-up behavior.

Open items for Hearth Health:
1) Data residency requirement — you mentioned US-only but wanted confirmation on region enforcement mechanics.
2) Latency SLO target — we proposed p95 < 300ms for API calls in the MAP; you signaled this might need tightening.
3) Procurement timeline — does your legal team need a separate MAP signature or will a single DocuSign covering the MAP + SOW suffice?

Next steps (proposal):
- Internal owners: please assign the Hearth owner for each exit gate (suggest a single point of contact per milestone).
- Redwood owners: Marissa will lead acceptance test orchestration, Ben will own infra provisioning, Laura will run the smoke-suite and capture evidence artifacts.
- We will iterate the MAP and deliver v2 by Wednesday after we get your priorities.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (draft MAP with timeline), acceptance-smoke-suite.csv (test rows), latency-slo-proposal.md (short rationale).

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai
Attachment stubs: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf), acceptance-smoke-suite.csv (text/csv), latency-slo-proposal.md (text/markdown)

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@hearthhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hearth Health Procurement <procurement@hearthhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 17:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan + Acceptance test catalog — next steps and owners

Thanks Sergio — this looks great and very actionable. Quick answers in-line: 

On data residency: Yes, US-only is mandatory. We run in a pair of AWS regions (us-east-1 primary / us-east-2 DR). We need the MAP to indicate which environment will hold test data and how it'll be purged post-eval.

On latency SLO: 300ms p95 would be excellent, but our product team wants to test 250ms p95 for the key search path. Can Redwood run a 250ms target for the pilot if we limit parallelism during the test window?

On procurement: legal prefers a single DocuSign envelope that includes the MAP as an appendix and the SOW. Procurement team (procurement@hearthhealth.com) will send redlines for the SOW next week.

Owners: I'll assign an internal owner for each milestone by EOD Monday — tentative contact is Andrew Li (will copy him once he is added).

One more ask: can Redwood provide a short template of the evidence bundle you expect for the SOC2 items? Helps speed internal approvals.

—Emily
Emily Chen
Head of Platform — Hearth Health
emily.chen@hearthhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Chen <emily.chen@hearthhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan + Acceptance test catalog — next steps and owners

Folks — quick internal alignment before I reply formally to Emily:

1) Data residency: We will provision a test cluster in us-east-1 and tag all containers/storage for a limited retention window (default 30 days). Laura, can you add the purge step to the acceptance evidence checklist and call out retention TTL?
2) Latency: Ben — confirm if we can hit p95 <= 250ms under constrained parallelism (e.g., 50 concurrent sessions) for the search path. If yes, we'll mark the pilot SLO 250ms p95 with the caveat that production may differ.
3) Evidence bundle: I've attached a short SOC2 evidence template we use internally (I will include as part of our v2 MAP). It lists logs, access control snapshots, architecture diagram, and test result archives.

Action owners (Redwood):
- Marissa: MAP v2 + DocuSign wrapper
- Ben: infra & region provisioning (us-east-1 primary)
- Laura: run smoke-suite, capture artifacts (results CSV, latency histograms, screenshots of dashboards)

I'll reply to Emily with the v2 timeline and include the SOC2 evidence template. Sergio, please note — we should be explicit in the MAP about accept/reject criteria for the pilot so Procurement has something to sign against.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Attachment stubs: redwood-soc2-evidence-template.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@hearthhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Hearth Health Procurement <procurement@hearthhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan + Acceptance test catalog — next steps and owners

Emily — thanks for the quick clarifications. Short reply and concrete next steps so Procurement has a clean handoff: 

- Data residency: confirmed — Redwood will run the evaluation in us-east-1 (test workspace). We will label and purge test data after 30 days unless you request a different TTL. That purge step will be a formal exit gate artifact.
- Latency: Ben confirmed (copied) that we can target p95 <= 250ms for the search path under a controlled pilot with capped concurrency; we'll capture p50/p95/p99 histograms as part of the smoke-suite evidence.
- Procurement/DocuSign: Marissa will package the MAP v2 as an appendix inside the DocuSign envelope. Procurement team, expect the envelope by Wednesday with the MAP as Appendix A.
- SOC2 evidence: attaching the evidence template Marissa mentioned; we'll populate it with the specific artifacts (logs, access snapshots, architecture diagram, smoke-test results).

Planned delivery: MAP v2 + DocuSign envelope by 2026-07-08 COB. Laura will run an initial smoke-suite run once the test workspace is provisioned and share results.

If that timeline works, we'll treat signatures (MAP + SOW) as the trigger to schedule the pilot activation window in Week 5.

Thanks everyone — I'll send the MAP v2 as soon as Marissa signals it's ready.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.ai
Attachment stubs: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (application/pdf), redwood-soc2-evidence-template.pdf (application/pdf)
